subject: Post-demo: privilege review + support on-call escalation playbook
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Bethany Lopez <bethany.lopez@arkfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Post-demo: privilege review + support on-call escalation playbook

Hi Bethany — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side focused on the data handling / support access topics you flagged. Attaching the set of questions you shared (arkfin-questions.xlsx).

Key points from the call (short):
- PII surface: customer-provided datasets + inferred attributes from LLM outputs. Ark currently expects masked PII retention <= 90 days and ability to purge on request.
- Data residency: primary region us-east-1; you asked about EU/secondary replication options.
- Logging and audit: requirement for immutable audit logs with 365-day retention for security events, token-level request traces stored for 90 days.
- Support access: least-privilege role model for support engineers, ephemeral JIT (just-in-time) elevation for troubleshooting, formal break-glass with approval workflow and full session recording.
- Compliance evidence: SOC 2 reports + config screenshots, plus runbook for break-glass and revocation timelines.

Open asks / proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm Ark's minimum required retention for token-level traces vs. aggregated logs (we noted 90 vs. 365 days)?
2) Confirm whether support engineers require remote access to any Ark-managed hosts (you indicated "no" but wanted to double-check for integrations).
3) Security call: propose Tue 11/10 10:00 AM ET for a 30-min call to walk Ark security through our support escalation playbook and evidence artifacts.
4) We'll produce a short support-access runbook (v1) and a one-page privilege matrix mapping Redwood roles -> Ark data scopes by EOD Monday.

If that aligns, we'll kick off the compliance packet prep and schedule the security walkthrough.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber

Redwood Inference

From: Bethany Lopez <bethany.lopez@arkfin.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ark Finance Security <security@arkfin.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: privilege review + support on-call escalation playbook

Jonas — appreciate the thorough recap. A few clarifications from Ark security and procurement: 

- Retention: For compliance, we need immutable security/audit logs retained for 365 days. Request traces that contain any PII-derived tokens must be deletable on request and can be retained for a max of 90 days. That split works if you can guarantee a deletion workflow tied to a request ticket.
- Support access: Correct — we do not give vendors access to Ark-managed production hosts. Any support troubleshooting needs to happen via your platform interfaces (debugging APIs, log bundles) or via temporary read-only tokens that Ark provisions.
- Break-glass: We require a two-person approval (one from Security, one from Ops) and that session recordings are retained for at least 180 days. Also need evidence that the access is time-limited and that revocation is immediate on demand.
- Data residency: we will proceed in us-east-1 for phase 1 but need a written plan for EU replication before any EU plans.

Procurement timeline: aiming to complete vendor security sign-off by 11/20 and have legal start contracting the week of 11/22. If you can commit to the security walkthrough next week and provide the runbook + evidence summary, that will keep us on schedule.

Thanks — Bethany
Bethany Lopez
Head of Vendor Risk, Ark Finance
bethany.lopez@arkfin.com | +1 203-555-0187

Bethany / Jonas — following up with the technical clarifications and a proposed mitigation approach. High-level answers first, then specifics.

High-level: Redwood supports the retention split you described (immutable security logs 365d; token-level request traces 90d with purge workflow). Support access will be implemented as:
- Role-based access control (RBAC) with predefined roles: Support-ReadOnly, Support-Triage, Support-Escalation.
- JIT elevation via an internal approval flow; elevation creates a time-limited session with full session recording and audit entry.
- Break-glass path: two approvers required (Security + Ops), automated email + Slack approval, immediate revocation endpoint, and session exports stored encrypted.

Technical specifics (brief):
- Logging: all support actions logged to an append-only store; writes are signed and exportable to S3 for retention. Log integrity hash included in compliance packet.
- Deletion workflow: token-level traces are marked for deletion and routed through a ticket ID; deletion is auditable and irreversible after the operation.
- Encryption & keys: customer data at rest encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key in your account for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer dedicated KMS per account.
- Residency: no EU replication without formal request; we can provide a scoped replication playbook and timeline.

Attachments: I attached a draft support-access-runbook-v1.pdf (internal draft) that lays out the escalation steps, roles, and screenshots of the RBAC UI. We'll finalize after your feedback.

Proposed immediate plan:
1) Jonas to schedule security walkthrough Tue 11/10 10:00 AM ET (we can also do 4:00 PM if better for Ark).
2) Redwood provides the one-page privilege matrix + runbook v1 by EOD Mon 11/9.
3) Deliver SOC2 + config screenshots and hash of logs by 11/13 for Ark security review.

We can also run a short on-call simulation during the walkthrough to demonstrate break-glass approvals and revocation.

Thanks — Marissa
